primitives.name: Home-Court Whistle Gain
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our results indicate that the there is a bias towards the home team - particularly pronounced during the playoffs - but it has been reduced since the COVID19 pandemic.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\Delta_{\\text{home}}': 'net whistle gain for home team (dimensionless count)', '\\mathbb{I}_{\\text{benefit}}^{\\text{home}, i}': 'indicator function for home team benefit on play i (binary)', '\\mathbb{I}_{\\text{detriment}}^{\\text{home}, i}': 'indicator function for home team detriment on play i (binary)'}
primitives.assumptions: Bias manifests as systematic deviation from random assignment of whistle outcomes; temporal correlation in playoff vs regular season.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( \Delta_{\text{home}} > 0 \), implies positive home bias; \( \Delta_{\text{home}} < 0 \) suggests away bias.

layer2.mapping: The net whistle gain operator maps to a probabilistic kernel over referee decision space, enabling GSI to compute confidence regions for bias magnitude.
layer2.telemetry: Observed net whistle gain per game, aggregated over L2M datasets.

primitives.name: Player-Level Bias Accumulator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Furthermore, there is robust statistical evidence that specific players benefit from referee decisions more than expected from pure chance.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{B}_p': 'player-specific bias accumulator (dimensionless score)', '\\mathcal{T}_p': 'set of plays involving player p', '\\mathbb{I}_{\\text{call}}^{\\text{benefit}, i}': 'indicator for beneficial call on play i (binary)', '\\mathbb{I}_{\\text{call}}^{\\text{detriment}, i}': 'indicator for detrimental call on play i (binary)'}
primitives.assumptions: Players exhibit persistent bias exposure due to repeated interactions with same referees; statistical significance tested via Monte Carlo simulations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If \( \mathcal{B}_p > \epsilon \), then player p is biased toward; if \( \mathcal{B}_p < -\epsilon \), then player p is disadvantaged.

layer2.mapping: The player bias operator is isomorphic to a reward-weighted policy gradient in reinforcement learning, where referee decisions act as stochastic actions.
layer2.telemetry: Monte Carlo simulation p-values for each player's net benefit over baseline chance.

primitives.name: Racial Bias Nullifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: Finally, our analysis on racial bias indicates the absence of any bias.
primitives.assumptions: No systematic difference in foul calls based on player race; data sufficiently representative.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Null hypothesis of zero mean racial bias is accepted if confidence interval includes zero.

layer2.mapping: The nullifier operator defines a kernel over demographic subspaces, used by GSE to validate fairness constraints in real-time.
layer2.telemetry: Chi-squared test p-value for racial group parity in foul call outcomes.
